name: CA-DEL
description: The success of machine learning in drug discovery hinges on learning the relationship between chemical structure and biological activity. DNA-Encoded Library (DEL) technology can generate large-scale screening data, but its primary signal - high-throughput sequencing read counts - is an indirect and noisy proxy for molecular binding affinity. To support rigorous model development under this noisy supervision setting, we introduce CA-DEL, an open, multi-target, multi-modal benchmark focused on the homologous subtype selectivity challenge within the Carbonic Anhydrase (CA) family. CA-DEL contains DEL screens against three clinically relevant and highly homologous isoforms, CAII, CAIX, and CAXII, together with systematically generated 3D protein-ligand pose ensembles. Unlike benchmarks that primarily emphasize large-scale binary hit classification, CA-DEL is designed to test whether models can transfer from noisy DEL enrichment signals to high-fidelity biophysical measurements. We therefore construct a Sim-to-Real evaluation setting by pairing DEL-derived training data with ChEMBL-derived binding affinities (K_i) for validation and testing. Through extensive baselines, pose-quality analyses, leakage controls, and zero-shot transfer experiments, CA-DEL provides a controlled benchmark for studying 3D-aware learning, denoising, and homologous target selectivity in DEL data analysis.
